name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%

model.rationale: The district's +21 Democratic lean and the fundamentals pointing toward a low-30s Democratic margin make this safely Democratic, and markets price a Democratic win at 97%. Clark's $1.6 million raised plus $4.2 million in outside support against a Republican with no reported fundraising reinforces the picture.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower race or unexpected Republican outside spending would warrant a recheck.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. David Scott's retirement created an open seat, and state Representative Jasmine Clark emerged as the Democratic nominee after a competitive primary. She enters the general election with strong financial backing, including more than $4 million in outside support and no outside opposition spending.

Republican Jonathan Chavez has reported little fundraising, and no public general-election polls are available for the race. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. With the seat's deep Democratic tilt and Clark's resource advantage, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
